1.title: Linear Functions and Systems

district.status: remade from the Savvas form by the department; not yet received
district.note: No district Topic 1 form is on disk (district tag unknown). The teacher says the common assessment is this Savvas form with questions removed, aimed at the SAT and Precalculus, so every item is district 'unknown' until the form arrives.

1.notes: Items by lesson: 1-1 owns 1-4, 1-2 owns 5, 1-3 owns 6, 1-4 owns 7-10, 1-5 owns 11, 1-6 owns 12-14; every lesson is in the year plan (none skipped). 1-1 has no fast lesson or prep entry (taught before the fast format), yet it carries four items (range, domain in context, average rate of change, increasing interval), all DOK 2 and all on Examples 1, 4 and 5 of 1-1: review them before the test. 1-4 (brief, one Example) carries four items including DOK 3 item 7; its kept Example 3 answers item 8 and the recursive form of item 7, but item 9 (series sum, Example 7), item 10 (reasonable domain, Example 1's 'domain is the natural numbers') and item 7's skipped-month step (find d from a1 and a4, Example 4A) are not in the packet. DOK: the TE item analysis has no DOK 1 item; items 7 and 14 are DOK 3 and the rest DOK 2 (the earlier audit's DOK table is wrong). Savvas misprints: Form B item 11 key prints x = -1, x = -3 but the graph and the algebra give x = -1, x = 3; Form B item 3 prints the unit m/min although the x-axis is horizontal distance in m (the 0.375 value is right). Only one change is recommended, for 1-2 (keep Examples 1 and 5 instead of 1, 2, 3, 5); 1-2 has already been taught and quizzed, so it applies to the topic review and the next re-cut of the packet.

byItem.formA: Quinten's cross-country distance-time graph (piecewise linear from (0,0) to (8,13)): what is the range of the function, as an interval?
byItem.formB: Drone height vs. horizontal distance graph (piecewise linear from (-4,0) to (4,3), dipping to (0,0)): what is the range, as an interval?
byItem.satWhy: reading the y-values a graph reaches appears, usually inside an interpretation item
byItem.precalcWhy: domain and range from a graph is assumed fluent
byItem.note: 1-1 Example 1 (Understand Domain and Range: range of y = x^2 - 3 in interval notation); practice 18 and 23 are tagged SEE EXAMPLE 1. Range of a piecewise graph is also practised in 1-3 Example 2.

byItem.formA: Same graph: what does the domain [0, 8] tell you about the race? (A 13 miles long, B Quinten takes 8 hours, C break at the 7-mile mark, D fastest in the last 2 hours)
byItem.formB: Same graph: what does the domain [-4, 4] tell you about the flight? (A landed once, B flew 3 m high, C traveled 8 m horizontally, D flew 8 minutes)
byItem.satWhy: interpreting a graph's input values in context is a standard SAT move, though rarely named 'domain'
byItem.precalcWhy: domain in context is reviewed when modeling
byItem.note: 1-1 Example 1 Part B (airtanker: the domain [0, 20] seconds comes from the context). Distractor A in Form A and B in Form B is the range, the Example 1 domain/range vocabulary.

byItem.formA: Same graph: average rate of change over [0, 2], in mi/h (from (0,0) to (2,4))
byItem.formB: Same graph: average rate of change over [-4, 4] (from (-4,0) to (4,3)), printed unit m/min
byItem.satWhy: rate of change / slope read from a graph is a standard item
byItem.precalcWhy: average rate of change is the bridge to difference quotients
byItem.note: 1-1 Example 5 (average rate of change over [a, b] as the slope of the secant; Part B reads it off a piecewise rideshare graph); practice 22 and 27 are SEE EXAMPLE 5. Form B's unit label m/min does not fit the stem (Savvas misprint); the value is right.

byItem.formA: Over what interval is y = -|x - 2| increasing? (A (2, inf), B (-inf, 2), C (-inf, -2), D (-2, inf))
byItem.formB: Over what interval is y = -2 + |x - 2| increasing? (same four choices)
byItem.satWhy: intervals of increase are rarely asked
byItem.precalcWhy: increasing/decreasing intervals are assumed for every function family
byItem.note: 1-1 Example 4 (Identify Where a Function Increases or Decreases: g(x) = 2 - |x|, the same downward V); practice 21, 26 and 31 are SEE EXAMPLE 4, and 1-1 quiz item 4 is the parabola version. The vertex comes from the 1-2 translation rule.

byItem.formA: Identify the translations of f(x) = x^2 that give g(x) = (x - 5)^2 - 4 (choices pair up/down 4 with left/right 5)
byItem.formB: Identify the translations of f(x) = |x| that give g(x) = 2 + |x + 3| (choices pair down 3/up 2 with left/right)
byItem.satWhy: translations via f(x - h) + k are a standard Advanced Math item
byItem.precalcWhy: function transformations are assumed fluent
byItem.note: 1-2 Example 5 Part B is the same task (g(x) = (x - 4)^2 + 5: 4 right, 5 up); Example 1 (Translate a Function) teaches each translation and the sign rule; practice 13 (DOK 3, vertex (3, -6)) and 18-21 are Example 1, 29-32 are Example 5. 1-2 quiz item 4 (|x - 3|) is the same sign trap.

byItem.formA: Graph y = 3 for -2 <= x < -1; 2 - x for -1 < x < 0; 2 for 0 <= x <= 4 (open/closed endpoints)
byItem.formB: Graph y = -2 for 0 <= x < 1; 3 - x for 1 <= x <= 2; 1 for 2 < x <= 4
byItem.keyA: Closed (-2,3) to open (-1,3); segment from open (-1,3) to (0,2); y = 2 from (0,2) to closed (4,2)
byItem.keyB: Closed (0,-2) to open (1,-2); closed (1,2) to (2,1); y = 1 from (2,1) to closed (4,1)
byItem.satWhy: piecewise graphs are rare on the SAT
byItem.precalcWhy: piecewise functions are reviewed (absolute value, limits preview)
byItem.note: 1-3 Example 2 (Graph a Piecewise-Defined Function, three pieces with open and closed circles); practice 11-13, 16 and 25 are SEE EXAMPLE 2. Example 2 is cut in the PLC-aligned fast packet; kept Example 5 (step function) rehearses the constant pieces and endpoint circles. Form A leaves x = -1 out of the domain (both neighbouring pieces exclude it).

byItem.formA: Enzo's profit: $900 in December, $500 in January, -$300 in March (February skipped); write the recursive formula a1 = [ ], a_n = a_(n-1) + [ ]
byItem.formB: DMV wait times: 1 min (1st), 1.2 min (2nd), 1.6 min (4th person; 3rd skipped); write the recursive formula
byItem.satWhy: recursive notation is not tested; only the constant-difference idea appears
byItem.precalcWhy: recursive and explicit sequence definitions are assumed in the sequences and series unit
byItem.note: 1-4 Example 2 (Write a Function for an Arithmetic Sequence: recursive definition from listed terms) plus Example 4 Part A (find d from a1 and a later term: 18 seats in row 1, 26 in row 5). The DOK 3 step is the skipped term: March is a4, so d = (-300 - 900)/3 = -400. Example 3 Part B (kept) writes the same recursive form from an explicit one.

byItem.formA: Recursive a1 = 2, a_n = a_(n-1) + 7 (game-show prizes): write the explicit formula a_n = [ ] + [ ](n - 1) and find round 7
byItem.formB: Recursive a1 = 15, a_n = a_(n-1) - 2 (players left): write the explicit formula and find week 6
byItem.satWhy: a + d(n - 1) is a linear model, a common SAT form in context
byItem.precalcWhy: explicit sequence formulas are assumed
byItem.note: 1-4 Example 3 Part A (recursive a1 = 3, + 0.5 to explicit a_n = 3 + (n - 1)(0.5)); Try It 3a is the same task; evaluating a term is Example 4 Part B. 1-4 quiz item 3 is the explicit form from a context.

byItem.formA: Mya's drone flights 11, 22, 33, ..., 77 m: total distance (A 275, B 308, C 143, D 385 m)
byItem.formB: Manny's Pizza profit 4, 1, -2, -5, ..., -56 (hundreds of dollars): total profit (A -$77,700, B -$54,600, C -$54,200, D -$49,000)
byItem.satWhy: arithmetic series sums are rare on the SAT
byItem.precalcWhy: finite arithmetic series are assumed in the sequences and series unit
byItem.note: 1-4 Example 7 (Use a Finite Arithmetic Series: find a_n, then S_n = n(a1 + an)/2; Try It 7 is the stairs); the formula is built in Example 5. Form B needs n = 21 first (solve -56 = 4 - 3(n - 1)), the Example 6 Part B step. 1-4 quiz items 2 and 5 are the same skill. Cut in the one-Example packet.

byItem.formA: Theater, 12 chairs in row 1, 2 more each row, 10 rows: reasonable domain of f(n)? (A all positive integers, B multiples of 2 from 12 to 30, C integers 1 through 10, D integers 0 through 10)
byItem.formB: Theater, 20 chairs in row 1, 4 more each row, 15 rows: reasonable domain? (A all positive integers, B multiples of 4, 20-76, C integers 1-15, D integers 0-15)
byItem.satWhy: domain of a sequence model is rarely asked
byItem.precalcWhy: sequences as functions on the natural numbers are reviewed
byItem.note: 1-4 Example 1 states 'a sequence is a function whose domain is the natural numbers' and tabulates term number as the domain; no Example asks for a reasonable finite domain. Example 4 (auditorium rows, cut) is the context parallel. Distractor B is the range; D starts at row 0. The 1-4 fast packet's Practice a last line rehearses it.

byItem.formA: Use the given graph to solve |x + 3| - 1 = (x + 2)^2 (V with vertex (-3,-1) and parabola with vertex (-2,0))
byItem.formB: Use the given graph to solve (1/2)|x + 1| + 1 = |x| (two V graphs crossing at (-1,1) and (3,3))
byItem.keyB: x = -1, x = -3 (printed; the graph and algebra give x = -1, x = 3)
byItem.satWhy: solutions as intersection points of two graphs, including nonlinear ones, are standard
byItem.precalcWhy: solving f(x) = g(x) graphically is assumed throughout
byItem.note: 1-5 Example 1 Part B (solve |x - 4| = (1/2)x + 1 by graphing: read the x-coordinate of each crossing); practice 9-14 are Example 1 and 1-5 quiz items 1-2 are the same task with the graph to sketch. Form B key misprint: x = -3 should be x = 3.

byItem.formA: Solve x + 4y = 15, 2x - y = -15
byItem.formB: Solve 2x - y = 7, x - y = 10
byItem.satWhy: solving a two-variable linear system is a standard Algebra item
byItem.precalcWhy: linear systems are reviewed (matrices, partial fractions)
byItem.note: 1-6 Example 1 (Solve a System of Linear Equations by substitution); practice 15-18 print SEE EXAMPLE 1 (the item analysis lists them as 16-19); 1-6 quiz items 1 and 3 are the same skill.

byItem.satWhy: SAT systems are two-variable
byItem.precalcWhy: three-variable systems return with matrices in Precalculus
byItem.note: 1-6 Example 3 Part A (Solve a System of Equations in Three Variables by elimination); practice 21-22 print SEE EXAMPLE 3 (item analysis: 22-23) and 1-6 quiz item 5 is the same skill. Multiple choice, so substituting each choice also works. Example 3 is cut in the PLC fast packet (Oct 20).

byItem.formA: Dwayne: 1 loaf + 6 eggs = $4.45; Sheila: 1 loaf + 12 eggs = $5.65: write and solve a system for the bread and egg prices, then find Mina's cost for 3 loaves and 2 dozen eggs
byItem.formB: Emery: 8 necklaces + 3 bracelets = 172 beads; 1 necklace + 5 bracelets = 77 beads: write and solve, then beads for 4 necklaces and 7 bracelets
byItem.keyA: Bread $3.25 per loaf; eggs $0.20 per egg; Mina pays $14.55
byItem.keyB: 17 beads per necklace, 12 per bracelet; 152 beads
byItem.satWhy: writing and solving a two-variable system from a word problem is a standard SAT item
byItem.precalcWhy: modeling with systems is reviewed
byItem.note: Two-variable system in context (not three-variable as the earlier audit says): 1-6 Example 1's method (the solve step); the write-the-system step is Example 2's define-the-variables / write-the-constraints routine (Steps 1-2), which is why the word-problem practice items 29 (coins) and 30 (tiles) print SEE EXAMPLE 2 although they are systems of equations (the item analysis files them under a nonexistent Example 5). The DOK 3 parts are writing the system (the dozen = 12 eggs trap) and the follow-up cost.

1-2.why: Already taught and quizzed in October with Examples 1, 2, 3 and 5 (the teacher's record), so the keep flags stand. For a re-teach or the Topic 1 review the topic test argues for Examples 1 and 5 alone: topic item 5 (translations from g(x) = (x - 5)^2 - 4) is Example 5 Part B's exact task plus Example 1's sign rule, both DOK 3 practice items (13 and 17) survive, and only quiz items 2 and 5 would be lost.

1-3.why: PLC-aligned fast packet (Oct 22): kept as ruled. The topic test would argue for Example 2 alone (a brief lesson keeps one): it owns topic item 6 (graph a three-piece function with open and closed ends), while Examples 3 and 5 own no topic item and carry quiz items 1, 3 (Example 3) and 4, 5 (Example 5). Kept Example 5 does rehearse item 6's constant pieces and endpoint circles; give item 6 one review round (practice 11-13) before the test.

1-4.why: Each candidate owns one topic item outright: Example 3 item 8 (recursive to explicit), Examples 2 and 4 item 7 (recursive formula with a skipped term), Example 7 item 9 (series sum), Example 1 item 10 (domain is the term numbers); Example 3 also writes item 7's recursive form (Part B). On quiz items Example 3 carries graded items 3 and 4 and ties Example 7 (items 2 and 5, full Savvas quiz only); the tie-break gives Example 3 the concept summary's two forms and the lesson's only DOK 3 practice item (15), so the one-Example cut stands. No other Example owns a topic item, so the second slot goes on quiz items: Example 2 carries quiz items 3-4 against Example 3's item 5. Add one V-and-parabola pair to practice since item 11 Form A is not a V and a line.

1-6.why: PLC ruling (Oct 20) kept. The topic test would argue for Examples 1 and 3: Example 1 owns items 12 and 14 (DOK 3, a two-variable system in context) and Example 3 owns item 13 (three-variable system) and quiz item 5, while Example 2 (inequalities) owns no topic item and carries quiz items 2 and 4. Item 13 is multiple choice, SAT none and Precalculus medium, so substituting the choices in all three equations is a fair review substitute for restoring Example 3 Part A.

2.title: Quadratic Functions and Equations

district.status: remade from the Savvas form by the department; not yet received
district.note: No district (department) Topic 2 form is on disk. The teacher says (Oct 31) the department remade it from these Savvas forms by removing questions, aiming at the SAT and Precalculus, so every item is 'unknown' until the form arrives.

2.notes: All 17 items map to lessons the year plan keeps (2-1 to 2-7 all have fast lessons; none is skipped). The current keeps (2-1: 4, 5; 2-2: 2, 3; 2-3: 4, 5; 2-4: 3; 2-5: 3; 2-6: 1, 5; 2-7: 1, 5; the Oct 31 re-cut toward this test, PLC not yet met) teach 13 of 17; the pre-recut packets (2-1: 2, 4; 2-3: 3, 6; 2-6: 1, 3; 2-7: 3, 4) taught only items 1, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 12 (item 3 by the same vertex step). The four still cut are each reachable: 3 (the vertex step of 2-2 Examples 2 and 3), 8 (one whiteboard round on 2-4 Example 1B), 11 (the 2-2 vertex step and the 2-1 features) and 13 (the symmetric points put the vertex at the origin). The re-cut in 2-1, 2-3, 2-6 and 2-7 dropped Examples that taught graded short-form quiz items, so those short forms were regraded with it (each prep entry's quizFocus); in 2-3, Try It 4 is quiz item 3's exact function, so item 3 is the bonus. Not on the SAT: items 8, 9 and 12 (complex numbers); item 10 low. Transcription notes: the TE Form A item 1 reads vertex (-1, 8) while the Realize download reads vertex (1, 8) with the hole at 3 s, so the item is mapped by its skill; page 98's running head 'TOPIC 1' is a publisher misprint; Form A item 10 choice C prints -6 then -5 (key unaffected); Form B item 4 says 'frame' then 'painting'; Form A item 5's grid labels the time axis t although the prompt says x; Form B item 2's reflection across the y-axis is in no Example. The item-analysis skill codes are copied as printed even where they differ from the matching quiz item's code (item 7 F16 against quiz A29).

byItem.formA: Golf ball's distance from the hole is the right side of a parabola with vertex (-1, 8) (TE print; the Realize download gives vertex (1, 8), hole reached at 3 s); write it in vertex form y = a(x + h)^2 + k
byItem.formB: Toy car's speed: minimum 2 m/s after 3 s, 3 m/s after 5 s; write the parabola in vertex form
byItem.satWhy: vertex-form quadratic models from a stated maximum or minimum are a standard SAT Advanced Math item
byItem.precalcWhy: vertex form and its transformations are assumed fluent in Precalculus
byItem.note: Mapped by the skill (vertex form from the vertex and one point, in context), not by the TE/Realize wording difference. 2-1 Example 4 (Application: a hit ball reaches its vertex at 20 ft after 1 s from 4 ft; substitute the vertex and the point, solve for a) is the context parallel, and the Realize wording ('after 1 second the ball is at its maximum ... 8 feet') follows it almost word for word. Example 3 and Try It 3 (vertex (1, -4) through (-2, -1)) are the context-free version; lesson-quiz item 3 (vertex (9, -1) through (7, 7)) is the quiz parallel.

byItem.formA: Reflect f(x) = x^2 across the x-axis, then translate left 4 and down 2; write g as y = ax^2 + bx + c
byItem.formB: Translate f(x) = x^2 right 2 and up 3, then reflect across the y-axis; write g as y = ax^2 + bx + c
byItem.satWhy: SAT asks for transformed function equations and expanded forms, usually one transformation at a time
byItem.precalcWhy: transformations of parent functions are assumed fluent in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-1 Example 5 (Write an Equation of a Transformed Function: vertex form, then expand) with Try It 5b (reflection in the x-axis followed by a translation); lesson-quiz item 5 (right 3, down 5, expanded) is the quiz parallel. Form B's reflection across the y-axis is in no Example (only the RtI support for Example 5 reflects points across the y-axis).

byItem.formA: Inside of a glass follows f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 9; which point is the bottom (choices (-3, 0), (0, -3), (0, 3), (3, 0))?
byItem.formB: Underground pool follows f(x) = x^2 + 8x; which point is the bottom (choices (-4, 16), (0, 8), (-4, -16), (0, -8))?
byItem.satWhy: the minimum point of a quadratic in standard form is a standard SAT item
byItem.precalcWhy: finding the vertex from standard form is assumed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-2 Example 1 (Find the Vertex from a Quadratic Function in Standard Form: h = -b/(2a), then k = f(h)); lesson-quiz item 1 (minimum point of x^2 - 4x) is the same task, and Form B (x^2 + 8x, no constant) matches it exactly. Example 2 Step 1 and Example 3 Compute repeat the h = -b/(2a) step. Form A is also the perfect square (x + 3)^2, readable as vertex form (2-1).

byItem.formA: Rectangular painting, length 1 ft longer than the width, area 12 ft^2; what is the width?
byItem.formB: Rectangular frame, length 7 in. longer than the width, area 18 in.^2; what is the length (the prompt says 'painting')?
byItem.satWhy: area word problems that reduce to a factorable quadratic are a standard SAT item
byItem.precalcWhy: modeling with a quadratic and rejecting the extraneous root is reviewed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-3 Example 4 (Find the Zeros of a Quadratic Function, Application: set the model to 0, factor, discard the root the context forbids); the TE's Additional Example 4 for Example 4 is this task (length 5 in. longer than the width, area 50 in.^2, reject w = -10), and A29 is the skill code of lesson-quiz item 3 (projectile lands), Example 4's quiz item. Practice 43 (apartments 12 ft longer than wide, 1,053 ft^2, filed under Example 3) is the practice parallel; the factoring itself is Example 3.

byItem.formA: Rock dropped off a bridge, y = -4.9x^2 + 14 (m, s); graph it from the drop to the water (curve (0, 14) to about (1.69, 0), closed ends)
byItem.formB: Bird landing, y = (1/2)(x - 4)^2 (m, s); graph from time 0 to landing (curve (0, 8) to the vertex (4, 0), closed ends)
byItem.keyA: graph from (0, 14) to about (1.69, 0), closed dots at both ends
byItem.keyB: graph from (0, 8) down to the vertex (4, 0), closed dots at both ends
byItem.satWhy: SAT reads and interprets graphs of quadratic models but never asks students to draw one
byItem.precalcWhy: graphing a model on its contextual domain is reviewed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-2 Example 2 (Graph a Quadratic Function in Standard Form: vertex, y-intercept, symmetric point, sketch); lesson-quiz item 5 (graph the diver's path y = -7x^2 + 5x + 16 from the jump to the water) is the same task, and the 2-2 packet's Practice block already rehearses the contextual domain. Form B is in vertex form, so its vertex comes from 2-1 Example 2.

byItem.formA: Projectile from a 16-ft tower, y = -16t^2 + 64t + 16; graph it and give the maximum height
byItem.formB: Projectile from a 20-ft tower, y = -16t^2 + 32t + 20; graph it and give the maximum height
byItem.keyA: 80 ft; graph from (0, 16) through the vertex (2, 80) to about (4.24, 0)
byItem.keyB: 36 ft; graph from (0, 20) through the vertex (1, 36) to (2.5, 0)
byItem.satWhy: the maximum height of a projectile from its quadratic model is a standard SAT item
byItem.precalcWhy: the vertex as a maximum is assumed in Precalculus optimization and modeling
byItem.note: Needs both parts: the graph is 2-2 Example 2 (key features) and the maximum is Example 3 (Interpret the Graph: the vertex of a downward parabola is the maximum; Try It 3 water balloon). Lesson-quiz item 3 (pebble from a cliff, y = -16x^2 + 32x + 80, maximum height) is the quiz parallel; practice 21 (model rocket, SEE EXAMPLE 3) is the practice parallel.

byItem.formA: Ball thrown from the top row of a stadium, h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t + 80; how long until it hits the ground?
byItem.formB: Ball thrown from the top row of a stadium, h(t) = -16t^2 + 80t + 96; how long until it hits the ground?
byItem.satWhy: solving a projectile model for when the height is 0 is a standard SAT item
byItem.precalcWhy: zeros of a model in context are reviewed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-3 Example 4 (golf ball from a 32-ft level: set h = 0, factor out -16, reject the negative time); Try It 4 is the same stadium setting (baseball from the upper deck, h = -16x^2 + 32x + 128), which is also lesson-quiz item 3. The item-analysis code F16 differs from the quiz item's A29, but the task is Example 4's.

byItem.formA: Use square roots to solve x^2 = -25 over the complex numbers; select all solutions
byItem.formB: Use square roots to solve x^2 = -121 over the complex numbers; select all solutions
byItem.satWhy: complex numbers are not tested on the digital SAT
byItem.precalcWhy: complex roots of quadratics are assumed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-4 Example 1 Part B (x^2 = -9 gives +/- 3i); lesson-quiz item 1 (x^2 = -64, select all) is the same task. Example 6 (solve with complex solutions by factoring) reaches the same answers.

byItem.formA: Write (4 + i)(4 - i) in the form a + bi (choices 16 - i, 16 - i^2, 17, 8)
byItem.formB: Write 3i(5 - 3i) in the form a + bi (choices 6 + 8i, -9 + 15i, -6, 9 + 15i)
byItem.satWhy: complex numbers are not tested on the digital SAT
byItem.precalcWhy: complex-number arithmetic is assumed in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-4 Example 3 (Multiply Complex Numbers): Form A is Part B (conjugates, (3 - 2i)(3 + 2i) = 13) and lesson-quiz item 3 ((2 + 7i)(2 - 7i)); Form B is Part A (a monomial times a binomial, -2.5i(8 - 9i)).

byItem.formA: Solve 5 = x^2 - 10x + 35 by completing the square (choices 5 +/- i; 5 +/- i sqrt 5; -6 - i sqrt 6 and -5 + i sqrt 6; -5 +/- i sqrt 5)
byItem.formB: Solve -2 = x^2 + 2x + 8 by completing the square (choices -1 +/- 9i; -1 +/- 3i; 4 and 2; -1 +/- sqrt 10)
byItem.satWhy: the SAT uses completing the square only to rewrite forms; complex solutions are not tested
byItem.precalcWhy: completing the square is reviewed in Precalculus (circles, conics); complex roots come back with polynomials
byItem.note: 2-5 Example 3 (Solve a Quadratic Equation by Completing the Square, 0 = x^2 - 2x + 3 gives 1 +/- i sqrt 2); lesson-quiz item 3 (0 = x^2 + 6x + 13, -3 +/- 2i) is the same complex case. Both forms first move the left-side constant (x^2 - 10x + 30 = 0; x^2 + 2x + 10 = 0). Form A choice C is printed -6 then -5 (publisher misprint; key unaffected).

byItem.formA: f(x) = x^2 + 3x + 1: select all true (vertex form (x + 3/2)^2 - 5/4; the swapped form; minimum -5/4 at x = -3/2; domain all reals; range all reals)
byItem.formB: f(x) = x^2 + 5x + 4: select all true (minimum -9/4 at x = -5/2; vertex form (x + 5/2)^2 - 9/4; minimum at x = 5/4; range all reals; domain all reals)
byItem.satWhy: choosing the equivalent form that displays the minimum is a standard SAT Advanced Math item
byItem.precalcWhy: vertex form, domain and range are assumed fluent in Precalculus
byItem.note: 2-5 Example 5 (Write a Quadratic Equation in Vertex Form by completing the square, then the maximum or minimum); practice 43-48 (SEE EXAMPLE 5) are this task. The minimum, domain and range choices read the 2-1 Example 2 key features, and 2-2's h = -b/(2a) gives the vertex (-3/2, -5/4) without completing the square, so the item is reachable from 2-1 and 2-2. No lesson-quiz item parallels it.

byItem.formA: Solve x^2 + 3x = -4 with the Quadratic Formula, x = ([] +/- i sqrt[])/[]
byItem.formB: Solve x^2 + 5x = -8 with the Quadratic Formula, x = ([] +/- i sqrt[])/[]
byItem.satWhy: the SAT uses the Quadratic Formula for real roots only; non-real roots are not tested
